## Findings
- claim-1: For \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), Theorem 5.4 states that \(J_v\subseteq\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) is generated by each of the two indicated Schur intervals; each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2@L1382-L1421|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: The original paper labels minimality of these generating sets a conjecture and reports computation only for \(r\le4\) and \(q=n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1489-L1502|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: Assume the integral box-Schur/Pieri presentation: \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) is connected graded with integral Schur bases, truncated Pieri holds, and \(\Lambda_+J_v=A_+J_v\). If \(a=1,b=2\), then \[ J_v/A_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2, \] where \[ x_0=s_{i^j},\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})}. \] Consequently both Theorem 5.4 families \[ (x_0,x_1,x_2),\qquad (x_0,y_1,y_2),\quad y_1=s_{(i^j,1)},\ y_2=s_{(i^j,2)}, \] map to integral bases and are minimal generating sets.
## Strategy
Let \(\alpha=q-i\), \(\beta=r-j\), so \(\alpha,\beta\ge1\) and \(\min(\alpha,\beta)=1\). Work conditionally on the integral box-Schur/Pieri presentation of \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\), including the requisite integral Schur description of \(J_v\).

Put \(d=ij\). Theorem 5.4 supplies generation of \(J_v\) by
\[
x_0=s_{i^j},\qquad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\qquad
x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})}.
\]
Thus \(Q\) is generated over \(\mathbb Z\) by their images.

In degrees \(d,d+1,d+2\), establish completeness using
\[
A_1=\mathbb Zh_1,\qquad A_2=\mathbb Zh_2+\mathbb Zh_1^2,
\]
and the Schur shapes containing \(i^j\). The degree-\(d+1\) relation is
\[
h_1x_0=x_1+y_1,\qquad y_1=s_{(i^j,1)}.
\]
In degree \(d+2\), use
\[
P=u+x_2+z,\quad R=u+z+y_2,\quad T=z+y_2+w,
\]
where
\[
u=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})},\quad z=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1)},\quad
y_2=s_{(i^j,2)},\quad w=s_{(i^j,1,1)}.
\]
Here \(u=0\) exactly if \(\alpha=1\), and \(w=0\) exactly if \(\beta=1\). Also
\[
h_1^2x_0=P+T,
\]
so \(P,R,T\) account for all degree-\(d+2\) relations.

The complementary-column matrices are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
(\alpha,\beta)&\text{complementary columns}&\text{row matrix}\\ \hline
(1,1)&(z,y_2)&
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\\[1.2ex]
(1,\beta>1)&(z,y_2,w)&
\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}\\[1.2ex]
(\alpha>1,1)&(u,z,y_2)&
\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\1&1&1\\0&1&1\end{pmatrix}
\end{array}
\]
with determinants \(1,1,-1\), respectively. Hence these local relation lattices are saturated and leave, respectively, the free classes \(x_2\). Together with degrees \(d\) and \(d+1\), this gives conditional integral independence of \(\bar x_0,\bar x_1,\bar x_2\).

Since the source-backed Theorem 5.4 generation makes
\[
\mathbb Zx_0\oplus\mathbb Zx_1\oplus\mathbb Zx_2\twoheadrightarrow Q
\]
surjective, its graded kernel has zero degree-\(d,d+1,d+2\) parts by the preceding computations, and no other degrees occur in its domain. Conditional on the presentation hypotheses, this proves
\[
Q\cong\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2.
\]
The relations also give \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1\) and \(\bar y_2=\bar x_2\), so the second three-element family has the same basis property.

This is a global saturation argument via Theorem 5.4 generation, not the requested all-column unit-pivot elimination order.

## Gaps
- The exact integral Schur-span/Pieri presentation of \(J_v\), and the equality \(A_+J_v=\Lambda_+J_v\), are not source-grounded in the supplied evidence. The argument remains conditional on them.
- Completeness of the displayed low-degree Schur columns must be written from the assumed Schur-span description, including box-boundary omissions.
- No degree-compatible unit-pivot order eliminating every higher Schur column has been constructed.
- Consequently, although the conditional generation-plus-saturation argument can bypass global elimination, it does not literally meet the requested pivot-order construction.

## Next
- Ground or independently prove the exact integral presentation hypotheses.
- Write the degree-\(d\) through degree-\(d+2\) completeness proof and the three determinant computations as a standalone audited lemma.
- Construct, separately for \(\alpha=1\), \(\beta=1\), and \(\alpha=\beta=1\), an explicit order on all remaining box partitions and coefficient-\(1\) Pieri pivots; prove triangularity and that the selected pivot rows generate the full relation lattice integrally.
